overall: The AG found the Select Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law: the late notice amendment was reasonable, open-session discussion needed no executive session or individual notice, and the town secretary allegation was declined.

allegations.summary: Board amended its January 6 meeting notice within 48 hours to add a topic on the status of the Conservation Commission Agent and Chair.
allegations.key_passage: Since Chair Coburn only learned the day before the January 6 meeting that this was a concern needing attention, we find that the Chair did not reasonably anticipate this topic 48 hours in advance.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board failed to give him notice that he would be discussed at the January 6 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Because the discussions occurred in open session, the Board was not required to provide the complainant with individual advance notice that he would be discussed.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board discussed his reputation, character, and complaints against him in open session rather than in executive session.
allegations.key_passage: Even if these discussions related to the complainant’s reputation or character, or to complaints brought against him, the Board was not required to have such discussions in executive session

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the town secretary called a state agency without a Board vote; the AG declined to review this non-Open Meeting Law claim.
allegations.key_passage: Even if true, this allegation would not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law and we therefore decline to review it.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
